properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Causal latent-space world model of stimulus-conditioned human brain dynamics with a new 20-participant movie-fMRI benchmark.
Two-stage framework: latent dynamics learning by next-latent prediction with a causal predictor conditioned on stimulus actions, then rollout decoding to ROI fMRI with subject-specific heads.

properties.algorithm: Causal transformer predictor over latent brain states with AdaLN stimulus conditioning and SIGReg

properties.population: healthy adults watching movies in 3T fMRI
properties.decision: forecasting brain activity and studying brain dynamics

legacy_cells.B: NeuroWorld: A Latent Brain World Model for Stimulus-Conditioned Human Brain Dynamics
legacy_cells.C: Dong, Zijian, Zhou, Jianxiong, Ng, Kwun Kei, Balagtas, Jan Paolo Macapinlac, Li, Zhizhou, Chen, Zijiao, et al.
legacy_cells.S: Can future whole-brain fMRI responses during naturalistic movie viewing be forecast from a measured fMRI prefix under temporally available audiovisual/text stimulus input?
legacy_cells.T: SG-MIND recruited 20 adult participants aged 22–40 years (9 female); one withdrew after one session. The three-benchmark evaluation included 30 participants overall.
legacy_cells.AK: Video-JEPA 2 gigantic (video); Wav2Vec-Bert-2.0 (audio); Llama-3.2-3B (text), used as frozen pretrained stimulus encoders
legacy_cells.AM: Multimodal stimulus features are aligned to the fMRI TR grid and mapped to a stimulus-action token; the token conditions latent predictor blocks through adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN).
legacy_cells.AT: At test, initialize from one observed fMRI TR; thereafter propagate autoregressively without re-assimilation of new fMRI observations.
legacy_cells.AZ: Analyses characterize latent dynamics and functional organization, including ROI prediction maps, stimulus-modality profiles, alignment effects, and cognitive decoding.
legacy_cells.BL: fMRI TR grid: Algonauts 2025 1.49 s; CineBrain 0.80 s; SG-MIND 0.719 s per TR.
legacy_cells.BN: Past-only causal temporal mask; predictor at t attends only to latent states and stimulus-action tokens available through t.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated latent brain states decoded to ROI-level whole-brain fMRI responses.
legacy_cells.BT: Shared decoder trunk with subject-specific linear output heads.
legacy_cells.BV: LDL: next-latent prediction loss plus λ-weighted SIGReg; LRD: masked ROI-level mean-squared error on decoded rollout predictions.
legacy_cells.DN: Algonauts 2025; CineBrain; Singapore Multimodal Imaging & Naturalistic Dataset (SG-MIND)
legacy_cells.DQ: 30 participants across the three benchmarks; SG-MIND comprised 20 participants.
legacy_cells.DX: Teacher-forced one-step Oracle mean ROI-wise Pearson r = 0.5385 (Algonauts 2025).
legacy_cells.DY: At 20 TR: SG-MIND r=0.2190, Pearson=0.2107, Cls@Top10=0.8044; Algonauts random split r=0.2961, Pearson=0.2759, Cls@Top10=0.8462; CineBrain r=0.2928, Pearson=0.2817, Cls@Top10=0.7289. Algonauts random split at 50 TR: r=0.2701, Pearson=0.2470, Cls@Top10=0.6747; at 100 TR: r=0.2660, Pearson=0.2412, Cls@Top10=0.6488.
legacy_cells.EB: On Algonauts, 20-step mean ROI-wise Pearson r was 0.2759 with aligned multimodal stimulus actions versus 0.1137 under stimulus–brain mismatch; this tests sensory alignment, not treatment effects.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with linear, TRIBE-based, and MIRAGE-based baselines. At 20 TR, NeuroWorld exceeded the strongest listed baseline on SG-MIND (r 0.2190 vs 0.0725), Algonauts random split (Pearson 0.2759 vs 0.2535), and CineBrain (r 0.2928 vs 0.2400).
legacy_cells.EJ: BrainVista is tabulated for Algonauts season-6 from its original paper only (r=0.2183, Pearson=0.2090, Cls@Top10=0.7619); authors state its code was unavailable for reproduction.
legacy_cells.EK: Stimulus-modality combinations; aligned versus mismatched stimulus conditioning; autoregressive rollout versus teacher-forced Oracle.
legacy_cells.EL: Forecast metrics decline as autoregressive horizon increases; authors report lower predictability in anterior association regions. On CineBrain, causally masked TRIBE/MIRAGE variants fell below the linear baseline.
legacy_cells.ER: National University of Singapore ethics committee approval for SG-MIND: NUS-IRB-2023-141; written informed consent obtained.
legacy_cells.FL: ROI-level fMRI encoder maps observations to continuous latent brain states; a causal latent predictor uses past latent states and aligned multimodal stimulus tokens; Stage 1 jointly trains state and dynamics, then freezes them; Stage 2 autoregressively rolls out states and decodes ROI-level fMRI with a shared trunk and subject-specific linear heads; no planner.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces a two-stage latent brain dynamics model trained by next-latent prediction and evaluated through causal autoregressive fMRI rollout; adds SG-MIND and compares performance across three movie-fMRI benchmarks.
legacy_cells.FN: At 20 TR, NeuroWorld achieved best reported metrics across the three benchmarks: SG-MIND r=0.2190 / Pearson=0.2107 / Cls@Top10=0.8044; Algonauts random split r=0.2961 / Pearson=0.2759 / Cls@Top10=0.8462; CineBrain r=0.2928 / Pearson=0.2817 / Cls@Top10=0.7289. On Algonauts random split at 100 TR, r=0.2660 and Pearson=0.2412.
legacy_cells.FO: The study focuses on movie stimuli, ROI-level fMRI, held-out runs from previously observed cohorts, and subject-specific output heads; it does not evaluate independent cohorts or unseen participants.
legacy_cells.FP: Evaluate independent cohorts and unseen participants; improve subject adaptation efficiency; extend to longer and uncertainty-aware rollouts, additional naturalistic paradigms, and other neuroimaging modalities.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors argue that stimulus-to-response brain encoding models can leak future stimulus information and optimize response fitting rather than a transition-sufficient latent state for recursive causal-time prediction.
legacy_cells.FR: The demonstrated causal constraint is past-only temporal access to external movie stimuli, not causal identification of treatment effects. No alternative clinical interventions, counterfactual identification assumptions, action planner, prospective patient evaluation, clinical utility, or uncertainty calibration are demonstrated.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–10: title/abstract; Introduction and Related Work (pp. 1–3); Methodology, Problem Formulation, both training stages, and architecture (pp. 4–5); experimental setup, cohorts, preprocessing, and data splits (p. 6); results and Tables I–III (pp. 6–7); ablations, rollout analyses, and interpretation (pp. 7–9); conclusion, limitations, future work, and references (p. 10). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. notes:
NeuroWorld learns a causal latent brain-state transition from fMRI and multimodal movie stimuli, then decodes rolled-out latents to ROI fMRI with subject-specific heads. On three benchmarks (SG-MIND, Algonauts 2025, CineBrain) it exceeds causal-adapted baselines on all reported metrics at 20 steps (for example Cls@Top10 0.8044 versus at most 0.1210 on SG-MIND). Performance declines gradually to 100 TRs, a mismatch contrast shows dependence on aligned stimuli, and a held-out movie season behaves like the random split. Classified L2, core, R2 (retrospective). Source points: subjects shared across splits, baselines adapted by the authors, code not yet released.

Targeted visual gap review 2026-11-22 inspected Figure 1 (p1), Figure 2 (p2), Table I (p5), and Figures 8-9 (p9). Figure 1 illustrates strict temporal stimulus masking and next-latent rollout, which does not itself establish intervention-effect identification. Figure 2 and Table I agree on benchmark sample sizes 4/6/20. Table I gives total person-hours approximately 260/36/140.7, per-subject approximately 65/6/7 h, TR 1.49/0.80/0.719 s and spatial resolutions 2/2/2.5 mm for Algonauts 2025/CineBrain/SG-MIND respectively. Figure 8 visualizes multimodal-minus-best-unimodal Pearson r gains and cognitive term correspondence (spin test, FDR p<0.05); Figure 9 encodes validation-set relative text/audio/video performance as red/green/blue, with blends indicating overlap. These functional associations are not clinical validation or causal identification. Existing scientific assessments and numeric metric values remain unchanged.
